HEALTH INSURANCE

What is Health Insurance?

Health Insurance is a shield that protects you and your family from financial instability during health emergencies. Against the common misconception that Medical Insurance is only for the elderly or people with health risks, its necessity is indispensable for everyone. The best health insurance policy offers peace of mind in times of hospitalisation by taking care of your medical bills. 

 

Uncertainties like COVID-19 have taught us the necessity of medical insurance. On the other hand, with the continuous spike in medical inflation, a health insurance plan can save your day either by providing cashless treatments or reimbursements on the incurred medical expenses. The flexibility of our health insurance is such that it can be availed either on an individual or floater basis to get wide coverage.

IMPORTANCE OF INSURANCE

Why Do I Need a Medical Insurance Plan?

The rising medical costs and an ever-increasing number of diseases make health insurance a necessity. Today, while planning your finances, never miss out on adding health insurance to your list.

Lifestyle Changes

The rising health complications are linked to the current lifestyle and environmental pollution. This necessitates the importance of being secured with a mediclaim plan, which can shield your and your family from financial troubles.

Medical Inflation

The cost of healthcare has multiplied over the years. It is not wise to solely depend on your savings to cover your medical needs. With the best health insurance, you do not have to worry about medical expenses to avail quality treatment.

Ambulance Expenses

Like the hospitalisation cover, it is important that the transportation expenses of the person to the hospital are taken care of during health emergencies. It implies the necessity of a medical insurance plan which covers ambulance charges.

Pre & Post-Hospitalisation

When it comes to health conditions, one often thinks only about hospitalisation expenses. But what about the costs incurred before and after hospitalisation? A mediclaim plan covers such expenses, thus, relieving you from financial stress.

Annual Health Check-Up

Having a periodic health check-up helps you prevent various health problems. Besides providing cover for incurred medical expenses, Health Insurance policies also facilitate annual health check-ups that help keep your health on track.

COVID-19 Cover

Pandemics like COVID-19 remind us of the importance of health and the necessity of medical insurance. So, to be financially stable even during uncertainties, buying health insurance becomes essential.

Tax Benefits

Medical insurance is an essential investment for which you can avail the tax exemption. Under Section 80D of the Income Tax Act, 1961, a taxpayer can avail tax exemptions on premiums paid towards the mediclaim policies.

Cashless Treatment

Cashless treatments are available at the Network Facilities that work in agreement with the Insurance Company. The cashless treatment facilitates you to concentrate on your recovery rather than worrying about your medical bills.

Financial Assistance

Make sure not to miss out on Health Insurance while planning your finances. Insuring yourself and your family members will make it certain that you are financially backed up in times of need. Medical inflation is ever-rising, so a sudden medical emergency may drain your savings.

 

Covers Pre-Existing Diseases

Most medical insurance policies cover Pre-Existing Diseases. Any medical conditions or ailments from which the policyholder is already suffering before opting for the medical insurance policy is referred as pre-existing disease (PED).

CATEGORIES

Types of Health Insurance Plans

Health insurance has become essential for everyone irrespective of age. The benefits of the medical insurance policies differ based on their types. Choose the policy that suits your needs by knowing about their types.

Indemnity Health Insurance Plans

Indemnity health insurance plans compensate the actual incurred medical expenses both in terms of cashless treatment facilities as well as reimbursements. Such types of mediclaim plans are available on individual and floater basis. They provide coverage up to the opted sum insured.

Star Comprehensive Insurance Policy

Fixed Benefit Health Insurance Plans

Fixed benefit health insurance plans provide lump sum cover for critical illnesses such as cancer, chronic kidney disease, brain tumour, etc. Keeping in mind the financial hardships one may undergo during life-threatening critical illness, the policy also pays the insured in one go.

Star Critical Illness Multipay Insurance Policy

Top-Up Health Insurance Plans

Top-up health insurance plans provide additional cover even after the exhaustion of the sum insured of your existing policy. Sometimes the opted cover may not be sufficient to meet your medical needs. In such times, a top-up policy can reinforce financial protection by providing additional coverage.

Super Surplus Insurance Policy

KNOW WHAT IS COVERED

How to Choose the Right Medical Insurance Plan?

Buying a mediclaim policy is one of the best investments you ever make. But how to choose a plan that best fits your needs? Knowing the inclusions and exclusions help you choose the best medical insurance plan. Here are some ways that will guide you through the process.

Hospitalisation Expenses
Most medical insurance plans cover hospitalisation expenses such as room rents, ICU charges, surgery expenses, doctor consultations, etc. incurred on illness, injury or accidents.
Pre & Post-Hospitalisation
Understanding the impact of rising medical expenses, most medical insurance policies cover pre and post hospitalisation expenses related to in-patient hospitalisation.
Day Care Treatment
Technological advancements have reduced the time of surgeries and treatments that once took a lot of time. Hence, medical insurance policies cover Day Care treatments and procedures.
Domiciliary Hospitalisation
Some medical insurance policies also cover domiciliary treatments taken at home on the advice of the medical practitioner.
Organ Donor Expenses
Most medical insurance plans cover organ donor expenses. Organ harvesting and transplantation expenses are covered if the insured person is the recipient.
Road Traffic Accident
Accidents are unpredictable. Most mediclaim plans cover in-patient hospitalisations due to road traffic accidents.
AYUSH Cover
In addition to allopathic treatments, most medical insurance plans also cover alternative systems of medicines such as Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homeopathy.
Health Check-up
In addition to hospitalisation and other benefits, medical insurance policies also cover the expenses incurred for health check-up.
Automatic Restoration
What if your medical expenses exceed your sum insured? At such times, the restoration benefit restores 100% of your sum insured automatically after its full or partial exhaustion.
TAX DEDUCTION

Avail Tax Benefits

A health insurance policy not only covers your medical expenses but also saves you money on taxes. As medical insurance is an essential investment, Section 80D of the Income Tax Act, 1961 allows a tax deduction for the premium paid towards the plan. Here are a few additional advantages:

Tax Deduction for Paying the Premium

You can claim tax deductions of up to Rs. 25,000/- by paying a health insurance premium for yourself or your family. If you are paying the premium for your parents as well, you can claim a higher tax deduction of up to Rs. 1 lakh.

Tax Deduction for Health Check-Up

In addition to premiums, you can also claim tax deductions for expenses incurred towards preventive health check-ups as well. Under Section 80D of the Income Tax Act, 1961, you can claim income tax deductions up to Rs. 5,000/-.

ONLINE BENEFITS

Why Buy Health Insurance Online?

Buying a medical insurance policy online is loaded with benefits. Here are a few of them:

Easy to Compare

People have varying needs. You can compare the benefits of various medical insurance plans online and pick the right plan that suits your needs. You can also get an idea about premiums, which can vary based on the plans you choose and the number of people you add.

Cost-Effective

Getting a health insurance policy online can save you money. Most health insurance companies offer a discount on premiums for first-time online purchases of the policy. In addition, it also saves your time and effort as you can purchase the best mediclaim policy in just a few clicks.

Instant Quote

You can get the quote for the mediclaim policy online. All you have to do is select a health insurance plan and enter information such as age, health condition, etc. It allows you to compare premiums, coverage and exclusions based on your age and health factors.

At Your Comfort

Now you can buy the best health insurance in the comfort of your home. No more physical visits are required to enquire about the medical insurance plans and company as everything is available online.

Abundant Choices

You have numerous choices, as most medical insurance companies help customers buy health insurance online. Take your time to pick the right plan by analysing them in detail.

Liability

The terms and conditions for insurance are a bit hard to understand. Most medical insurance companies have listed the benefits of their policies on their website. This makes them trustworthy and easy to understand.

Transparency

Online processes are transparent. After completing the required information, you will proceed further to buy your health insurance policy. The premium is calculated based on your requirements. The online platform allows you to add or subtract the benefit, sum insured, your family members, etc. Based on your inputs, the premium is calculated and you can see the variation in the premium.

SECURE EARLY

Benefits of Buying Medical Insurance at an Early Age

There is no specific age for buying a health insurance plan. However, opting for a medical insurance plan at an early age has its advantages.

Less Premium

Age is an important factor in calculating the premium of Medical Insurance. The younger you are, the lower your premium will be.

Continuous Cover

Continuous cover through renewals will help you tide over the waiting period for Specific and Pre-Existing Diseases (PED).

Medical Test

Pre-insurance medical screening is not required if you purchase a health insurance policy at a young age.

No-Claim Bonus

You can avail a no-claim bonus for every claim-free year. It will enhance the sum insured that benefits you at later stages.

Co-Payment

No need to share your medical bills as co-payment is not applicable when you opt for a medical insurance policy at a young age.

Star Health Insurance plans provide more flexible benefits when the policyholder buys a mediclaim policy and goes through certain hardships. For instance, when the sum insured gets exhausted, additional coverage is provided without any extra premium. This is where benefits like Automatic Restoration of the basic Sum Insured, Super Restoration of the basic Sum Insured and Road Traffic Accident (RTA) on the sum insured come into place.

Note: These flexible benefits are product/policy specific. Please refer to the policy clause to learn more.

 

Health Insurance Plans Allow Additional Disease-Specific Coverage

 

With Star Health, the insured can avail disease-specific policies for critical illnesses, cancer and cardiac ailments along with inpatient hospitalisation as a general mediclaim health insurance policy. We have a wide range of mediclaim health insurance policies to choose from like  Star Cardiac Care Insurance Policy-Platinum, Star Cancer Care Platinum Insurance Policy and Star Cancer Care Platinum Insurance Policy.

 

Health Insurance Plans Cover Non-Hospitalisation Expenses

 

The insured can avail of non-hospitalisation expenses covered with most of our mediclaim Health Insurance Policies. Those include expenses, dental treatments, annual health check-ups, out-patient care treatments, diagnostics, consultations, etc.

 

Everything You Need To Know About The Mediclaim Policy

 

Steering the complexities of healthcare expenses in India can be quite overwhelming. With rising medical costs rapidly, a mediclaim policy works as a safety net and a critical resource. This article will direct you through the basic features of mediclaim policies, including mediclaim insurance and tips on choosing the best mediclaim policy in India.

 

What is a Mediclaim Policy?

 

A mediclaim policy is a health insurance policy which covers the medical costs incurred during hospitalisation and associated procedures. It gives financial assistance for medical exigencies, lowering the burden on the insured and their families. Mediclaim policy in India provides different benefits, which make them a favourite among individuals looking for financial protection in medical emergencies.

 

Main Aspects of Mediclaim Policy

 

Hospitalisation Coverage: Mediclaim insurance policies cover the cost of hospitalisation because of illness or injury. This consists of nursing charges, room rents, and other allied charges.

Pre and Post - Hospitalisation Expenses: Many mediclaim policies in India cover medical costs incurred during pre-and post-hospitalisation, ensuring encompassing coverage for the treatment process.

Daycare Procedures: Few medical procedures do not involve prolonged hospitalisation and can be treated within a few hours. Mediclaim policies even cover such daycare procedures.

Annual Health Check-Up: Certain mediclaim insurance policies provide the facility of an annual health check-up, motivating people to undergo regular health checks.

Cashless Facility: Many insurance providers provide cashless treatment at network hospitals, saving the insured from making out-of-pocket payments.

Outpatient Department (OPD) Cover: Some mediclaim policies cover outpatient treatment, such as diagnostics, consultations, and minor procedures without hospitalisation.

No Claim Bonus: If the policyholder doesn’t make any claims during the policy term, they are entitled to a no-claim bonus, either as a reduction in the premium or an increase in the sum insured for the next policy year.

Alternative Treatments: Many policies today cover alternative treatments like Ayurveda, Yoga, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy (AYUSH). This works with the needs of those who want traditional and holistic medical treatment.

 

Tips to Choose the Best Mediclaim Policy


Coverage: The policy must have an exhaustive list of medical conditions and treatments.

Network Hospitals: See if the insurance provider has a large network of hospitals where you can get cashless treatment.

Claim Settlement Ratio: Choose an insurance provider with a good claim settlement ratio, which shows its ability to settle claims.

Additional Benefits: Choose plans with extra benefits, such as wellness programs and health service discounts.

 

Exclusions in Mediclaim Policies

 

Pre-Existing Diseases: Many policies exclude coverage for pre-existing diseases after a waiting period.

Cosmetic Treatments: The cosmetic or beauty treatment expense is not typically covered.

Self-Inflicted Illnesses: Any illness or injury caused due to self-inflicted injury or suicidal attempts is not covered.

 

How to Make a Claim

 

Intimate the Insurer: Notify the insurance provider immediately of the hospitalisation or medical treatment.

Documents to Submit: Please submit all the documents, including medical reports, bills and discharge summaries.

Cashless Claims: If you use a cashless facility, ensure the hospital is in your insurer’s network and use the procedure for pre-authorisation as required.

Reimbursement Claims: Your insurer can reimburse you for your medical bills and reports for non-network hospitals.

 

Conclusion

Choosing the best mediclaim policy is essential to ensure your family’s health and financial security. Comprehending the different dimensions of mediclaim insurance will help you choose the best for you. Investing in a good mediclaim policy is a step towards a healthier and financially secure future.

Key factors to consider before buying your Health Insurance Policy

 

Choosing the best Health Insurance is quite a task. It is hard to pick the best health insurance plan in India while numerous firms are offering Health Insurance. The inclusion and exclusion differ from each policy. Every information that you gather will help you in the process of choosing the right Health Insurance Plan.

When it comes to choosing the best Health Insurance Policy, be mindful of the following:

 

Inclusion and exclusion are the key factors, so it is important to read them carefully before opting for the policy. This can avoid misconceptions during the claim process. Understanding your Health Insurance coverage gives you an upper hand while filing a claim.

 

Waiting Period in Health Insurance should be of major concern because, during the waiting period, you cannot raise a claim to avail the benefits. Thereby, it is essential to know the duration of waiting periods. It is advisable to choose a policy that has a lower waiting period.

 

Network Hospitals are the hospitals that work in agreement with Insurance Companies to provide cashless treatment. Go for the insurer who has a wide network of hospitals as you can choose the one that suits you best.

 

Co-payment refers to the sharing of medical bills between the insured and the insurer. Some policies make co-pay mandatory and for some it is optional. Being aware of your co-pay gives you more flexibility while planning your finance.

 

Sub-limits are a common factor in Health Insurance. The policy might have sub-limits for different expenses such as room rent, Domiciliary treatment, AYUSH treatment, Cataract treatment, etc. So, the claim amount for such expenses is covered up to the mentioned sub-limits and you have to pay the balance amount.

 

A cumulative Bonus is also known as no-claim bonus. If you do not raise a claim during the policy period, then your Sum Insured will be enhanced by certain percentage. Such enhancement is called a cumulative bonus. The accumulated bonus will come in handy during the needful times.

 

How to choose the best health insurance options available in India?

 

Finding a single health insurance policy that caters to all your needs is impossible. There are several policies available, each with its own set of unique benefits. Therefore, it is essential to carefully evaluate the coverage benefits of each policy and determine what is included and excluded before selecting the best health insurance in India.

 

Checking waiting period for pre-existing diseases 

 

Each health insurance plan has specific terms and conditions for pre-existing conditions. This implies that if an individual has any illness before obtaining a plan, the claim made for treatment of that particular illness will only be accepted after the insured has completed a specified waiting period. 


Typically, the waiting period can vary between 6 months to 3 years, although specific superior plans, such as the mediclaim policy, offer a shorter waiting period. When selecting a health policy, choosing one with a shorter waiting period is advisable.

 

Check customer reviews 

 

When purchasing medical insurance online, it is imperative to consider customer reviews of various health insurance companies. These reviews provide a balanced mix of positive and negative opinions, highlighting the relevant pros and cons. This valuable information will enable you to make a well-informed decision. 


Compare premiums 

 

It is essential to conduct a thorough comparison of both the plans and the premium. Numerous online aggregators exist that assist in comparing insurance policies based on their benefits, features, premiums, maximum returns, and more. Selecting a plan without carefully considering all available options in the market is akin to inviting future regret. By comparing plans, you can secure all the benefits at a relatively lower premium rate.

 

Read exclusions 

 

Policyholders must pay more attention to exclusions in a health insurance policy, leading to unexpected situations. While a plan may cover certain illnesses, it is essential to note that there are limitations and exclusions. For example, some strategies may exclude coverage for conditions like hernia, cataract, sinusitis, Gastrointestinal issues, and joint replacement during the initial period. Additionally, expenses related to dental treatment, HIV/AIDS, eye-related healthcare, STDs, and cosmetic surgery may also be excluded. Selecting a health plan with fewer exclusions is advisable to ensure comprehensive coverage.

Factors to Consider When Selecting a Health Insurance Company in India


You can shortlist the top 5 medical insurance companies in India before you choose one to buy your health insurance plan from. Here are some of the factors that influence the selection of a health insurance company in India. 


1. Claim Settlement Ratio
Select the insurance companies with the Claim Settlement Ratios. Claim Settlement Ratio (CSR) denotes the percentage of claims settled by an insurance company in a year compared to the total claims obtained annually. A high CSR denotes that the insurance company has a record of settling claims. 
2. Company’s Solvency Ratio
The solvency ratio means the surplus of assets over liabilities and other obligations of the health insurance company. In general, a high solvency ratio denotes the reliability, stability, and long-term financial security of the company.   
3. List of Network Hospitals 
When choosing health insurance, thinking of the network hospitals (both in-patient and out-patient facilities) is essential as it affects the convenience, cost, and quality of healthcare services available to policyholders. 
Having access to several hospitals ensures easeness and accessibility to healthcare services. Policyholders can select from a set of provided network hospitals, which have reputed medical facilities, for their medical treatment requirements. 
4. Coverages Offered
Consider the various coverage options available, like hospitalisation, critical illness coverage and cashless treatment. Look for health insurance plans with comprehensive hospitalisation coverages and a minimum number of exclusions.   
5. Policy Exclusions 
Understand the health insurance policy exclusions clearly to ensure you know what is not covered by the health insurance plan. Many health insurance policies exclude pre-existing diseases or other medical conditions that policyholders already have at the time of buying the policy.
Also, health insurance policies may exclude coverage for congenital diseases or conditions present at birth.
6. Customer Service Reputation 
Consider the customer service reputation when buying health insurance so that you can choose an insurance provider that provides reliable support, transparent processes, and a commitment to customer satisfaction. 
7. Claim Process Easiness
An easy claim process ensures that you get a good experience with your health insurance provider and can concentrate on your healthcare without have to worry about the hassleness of claims.
8. Premium Affordability
Make sure that you choose an affordable premium for you. Clearly understand the premium affordability criteria set by the insurer or employer to make sure that the health insurance premium fits within the budget constraints of the policyholder.

 

Generally, medical insurance comparison also helps find out the best medical insurance.  

 

Benefits of Medical Insurance Policy   


There are many medical insurance plans in India. There are many benefits that policyholders can get from the medical health insurance plans. Here are the benefits of buying a Medical Insurance plan. 


1. Insurance Coverage During Medical Emergencies 
Medical Insurance Policy covers the expenses of various healthcare needs. This can include doctor fees, regular checkup visits to the hospital, major surgeries, etc. One of the best benefits of health insurance is the cashless treatment facility. During emergency hospitalization, you might not have enough amount to pay for the expenses immediately. At that time, medical insurance helps you get proper healthcare without having to worry, as the network hospital can settle the bills directly with the insurer. The policy terms will lay down the particulars of the health insurance benefits at the purchase time.   


2. Flexible Premiums for Individuals
The benefits of medical insurance advantages can be useful if you have planned for it beforehand. By doing so, you provide a sufficient time period to spread the premium over the years and also lower the financial stress.  
If you do not have an insurance policy in place, it might drain your savings. So, it is better to wait for a medical emergency to buy a health plan. 


3. Protection against Medical Costs 
The increase in healthcare costs is making people fear. To avoid being stressed by medical costs, the benefits of health insurance have become valuable.  
When you add a health insurance policy to your financial plan, it can save you. The assurance of security against rising healthcare charges is among the advantages of health insurance.  

  
4. Offers Riders or Various Life-related Uncertainties
Riders are the most valuable benefits of medical insurance. Other than the medical insurance benefits, you can enjoy multiple coverage options. Such health insurance advantages help to create a personalized financial plan.
For example, a critical illness insurance rider could offer proper medical insurance coverage against a list of life-threatening diseases that require high healthcare costs. 


5. Extra Coverage Above Employer Health Insurance
Several companies provide employer health insurance benefits to their employees. While they are useful, you might not have to depend on anyone for money in a time of need. Since the benefits of health insurance provided by a company are below a master policy, there are limitations to individual coverage. 
When you purchase an individual plan, you can avail yourself of extra health insurance benefits that are specific to your requirements.


6. Tax Benefits
Apart from giving many benefits, health insurance also helps save on taxes. The Indian government permits the policyholder to lower their tax liability when they buy a health plan. Below Section 80D, there are specific tax benefits of health insurance applicable to a few conditions. However, the tax advantages are as prevailing tax laws subject to change.   


7. Covers Pre- and Post-Hospitalisation Expenses
Apart from hospitalization expenses like ICU charges, surgical procedures, etc., health insurance plans often offer coverage for the expenses incurred during the pre- and post-hospitalization periods. These health plan benefits are subject to various terms and conditions, so check the policy documents for applicable inclusions and exclusions in regard to these expenses.


8. Offers Maternity Cover Benefits
Maternity coverage is provided as an extra add-on in most health insurance plans. Maternity coverage in health insurance can help offer coverage to many child-birth-related costs like a hospital stay at the time of childbirth, doctor visits, cesarean/natural delivery, etc. This permits expectant parents to concentrate on the mother and their child’s health without the additional financial stress.  


9. Covers the Cost of Ambulances  
Your health insurance plan might cover the ambulance ride cost to the nearest hospital during an emergency. This can save you money and help you get the necessary medical treatment faster. This health insurance benefit could help you claim reimbursement for the ambulance charges as per the terms and conditions of your medical insurance policy.    


10. Annual Checkup Benefits  
Many health insurance policies include annual checkups as a complimentary advantage below the policy. This could be beneficial as it can help you find out the health issues early on, making them easier to treat. These checkups include physical exams, blood tests, and other screenings. By having regular checkups, you can find out serious health problems at an early stage and take proper action correctly.    


11. Day Care Treatment Coverage 
A number of treatments that earlier needed hospitalization can now be completed through modern outpatient daycare procedures. Several medical health insurance plans currently provide reimbursement for modern treatments like balloon sinuplasty, stereotactic radio surgeries, oral chemotherapy, etc., that do not need hospitalization.  
As the list of these covered daycare modern procedures differs in various health plans, read through the policy documents to learn what is covered below your health plans.

How to claim Medical Insurance? 


Know the medical insurance claims processing steps. Medical claim insurance has simple steps. To claim health insurance, you can follow these steps:

  • Make sure that you inform the insurer of your upcoming expenses within the particular time period in your policy.  
  • Finish filling out the claim form correctly and get it signed.  
  • Collect the necessary documents like :
    1. Original bills, receipts, and discharge papers from the hospital.  
    2. Doctor's prescription copy and referral letter 
    3. Diagnostic test reports
    4. Medical reports 
    5. Original bills received from pharmacy/chemists 
    6. Police FIR if it is a personal accident 
    7. Policy Copy(Very important) and medical insurance card. 
    8. Policy holder’s ID card
  • Submit all the necessary documents to the insurer. 
  • Check claim status online through the insurer's website or mobile app. 
  • If all the procedures are correct, the insurer will reimburse you for the medical expenses amount spent.

 

What is a Medical Indemnity Insurance? 


Medical indemnity insurance saves medical professionals from financial losses because of medical malpractice or negligence. It offers coverage for legal costs and compensation payments. This is also called professional indemnity insurance. 


How does it work? 

 

  • It offers coverage for legal costs and compensation payments. 
  • This Medical Indemnity Insurance helps safeguard against financial losses from allegations of negligence or malpractice.  
  • It covers the cost of investigations, appointing a lawyer, or other legal expenses.
  • It covers the cost of defending oneself in court.

Health Insurance terms you need to know about

It is important to know about certain terms before purchasing health insurance. These terms help to know more about the policy coverage and its criteria. It is important to go through all the terms to avoid major mistakes. However, some terms can be difficult to understand.

Some of the general and common terms that will help you choose the correct health insurance plans are given below.

 

1. Sum-Insured

 

Sum-insured is the policy coverage amount.

 

2. Premium

 

Premium is the amount you must pay the insurer or the health insurance company against the policy purchased. The premium will depend on the type of policy you choose, the policyholder, age and other factors.

 

3. Cashless Claims

 

Cashless claims are health insurance claims that can be availed in the insurer’s network hospitals.

 

4. Add-On Covers

 

Add-on covers are additional features that offers additional financial covers in health insurance against unknown medical emergencies that involves high medical costs.

 

Other names for add-on covers are riders and optional covers. Critical illness, room rent waiver, maternity cover and hospital cash benefit are some of the common add-ons that can enhance your base health insurance.

 

5. Critical Illness

 

Critical illnesses are life-threatening medical conditions like kidney failure, cancer and cardiovascular diseases. For such critical illnesses, there are special plans that cover these illnesses. Additionally, you can get an add-on or a rider cover.

 

6. Network Hospitals

 

All health insurance companies have a tie-up with a certain number of hospitals in the country. These tie-ups with hospitals are called network hospitals.

 

7. Automatic Restoration

 

Most health insurance companies are offering automatic restoration benefits. You will benefit from insurance backup when you have exhausted the sum insured. In automatic restoration sum insured gets reloaded for the next hospitalisation during the policy term.

 

8. Pre-Existing Disease/Co-Morbidities

 

Co-morbidities like hypertension, COPD, kidney diseases, diabetes and other major health issues are considered as risk factors for health insurance. So people with any of the co-morbidities mentioned above are charged a higher premium.

 

9. Exclusions

 

Exclusions or limitations are circumstances and conditions that health insurance companies will mention in their policy wordings clearly. In such cases, your health insurance claims can get rejected or will not be processed further.

 

10. Inclusions

 

Inclusions or coverage benefits are one section that you should check properly. These benefits refer to benefits and other policy features the insurer will compensate you. Some common inclusions include hospitalisation, anaesthesia, surgery, ambulance charges and treatment-related expenses.

 

11. Waiting Period

 

In medical insurance, there will be a waiting period for health conditions. During the waiting period, you cannot avail the health insurance claims. The waiting period will differ for various health conditions and insurance policies.

 

12. Top-Up Plans

 

Top-up plans are policies that can be bought along with the base policy. When the sum insured by the base policy gets exhausted, the top plans will cover you.  

 

13. Co-Payment

 

A copay clause or co-payment is a fixed percentage of the amount the policyholder should pay to the hospital on the expenses in the treatment taken. Copay percentage differs from policy to policy and depends upon the entry age.

What are the optional add-ons in Health Insurance?

Add-ons or optional features in health insurance can be included in your base policy by paying an additional amount at purchase. In most cases, people choose ad-ons as they are cost-effective and also have significant advantages.

Also known as health insurance riders, add-ons help you avail extra benefits and increase the scope of your current medical insurance policy. Add-ons are highly recommended assets that are worth investing in, as they will allow you to acquire the best health insurance for the future.

What are the Health Insurance eligibility criteria?

Health insurance plans has different eligibility criteria, including age, pre-existing medical conditions, etc. The following conditions must be met to qualify for a health insurance plan. 

 

  • Age

 

The entry age for adults is 18, and they are eligible for all benefits according to the terms and conditions of the policy. However, the age criteria vary for different policies.

 

  • Pre-Medical Screening

 

The pre-medical test is a must for policyholders over the age of 45 or 55. However, prior to issuing a policy, most senior citizen health plans need medical exams.

 

  • Pre-Existing Disease (PED)

 

Pre-existing conditions are diseases diagnosed in the insurer before purchasing the health insurance plan. Pre-existing diseases have a set waiting period during which you are not eligible for all your health insurance benefits.

 

You can submit claims for that specific condition under your health insurance plan only after the waiting period. To prevent claim denial, provide the right information about your health issues and lifestyle choices

Health Insurance Premium Calculator: An Overview

 

Health insurance premium is defined as the amount of money you have to pay to the insurer on a periodic basis to avail medical coverage as and when required. A health insurance premium calculator enables you to calculate your mediclaim premium based on the customer’s requirements.

 


The insurer is liable to pay for the medical bills and hospitalisation expenses when the insured is diagnosed with any ailments subjected in the policy terms. Here are some of the benefits of an online health insurance calculator:

A health insurance premium is calculated based on the entry age with gender, medical history, policy terms, no-claim bonus, and lifestyle factors.
 

Several factors influence your health insurance plan, affecting whether the premium of your health insurance policy increases or decreases. Mentioned below are some of these factors:

 

  • Age

 

Age determines the health insurance premium. The higher the age, the higher the premium for the health insurance plan. With an increase in age, you are more prone to developing age-related diseases and require medical care, which raises the premium of your health insurance coverage.

 

  • Medical History

 

The premium for the policy increases when there is a pre-existing disease.

 

  • Duration of the Policy

 

The length of the health insurance policy will impact the premium of the plan. The premium tends to be lower for a higher-duration policy.

 

  • Habits

 

You are more likely to experience significant health problems if you smoke, drink, etc. These lifestyle habits affect the health insurance premium.

 

  • Occupation

 

The nature of your occupation or work influences the health insurance premium. The premium increases if you work in a harmful environment or have a stressful job.

 

  • Body Mass Index

 

Diabetes, obesity, heart disease, etc., are related to the BMI index. The insurance premium is higher for those with high BMI indices.

  • Select Family Floater Plans

 

Although the needs for health insurance are unique for every individual, these plans are made to fit all the members of a family.

A family-floater plan pays for all family members’ medical bills. However, it is considerably less expensive than if you had to purchase a separate plan for every member of your family.

Any family member who needs it due to an urgent medical situation may use the money assured under the plan.

 

  • Maintain a Healthy, Active Lifestyle

 

Your lifestyle significantly impacts the premium for your health insurance plan. Life-threatening diseases are less likely to affect those who don’t smoke, drink, use tobacco, or use drugs. As a result, people who lead healthy lifestyles get minimal premiums.

Busting Myths about Health Insurance

#1 People in good health don’t require health insurance

You can reap the long-term benefits of health insurance even when you’re healthy and young. Health insurance protects you from any unforeseen health.

 

#2 Insurance doesn’t cover pregnancy

There are insurance policies with maternity coverage subject to certain terms and conditions. 

 

#3 Your entire medical expenses will be reimbursed

The amount of reimbursement depends on the policy. Most plans cover room charges based on the sum insured, and any excess must be paid by the insured. A policy may have sub-limits for other costs which are subject to partial reimbursement. 

 

#4 Online health insurance purchases are not safe

Health insurance sales have gradually increased online. However, many believe that online transactions could result in fraud. This is untrue since insurers have launched online portals for easier policy purchases.

In case of unplanned hospitalisation, you can contact the insurance company after being admitted.

As per the insurance policy clause, the insurance company will provide coverage for both planned and unplanned hospitalisations.

Yes, you can claim medical bills without hospitalization through health insurance if your medical health insurance plans cover OPD or domiciliary hospitalization.   
 

Yes, you can purchase health insurance without a medical test if you are under a particular age and do not have pre-existing conditions. But it's better to get a medical examination before you buy health insurance. 
 

Below Section 80D of the Income Tax Act, you can avail of a tax deduction of a maximum of Rs 25,000 every year for medical insurance premiums. When you buy health insurance, you could ask about the details of the medical insurance deduction. 
 

Medical insurance for pregnancy, also called maternity insurance, is a health insurance plan that offers coverages for pregnancy-related expenses. It can include prenatal care, delivery, and postnatal care.
